issues.legal_issue: A lessee whose estate has been notified is entitled to the rent collected under the applicable rent-reduction regime, not to any greater amount assessed as land revenue under a later ryotwari settlement.
material_facts: The appellants held leasehold rights in lands in an estate that was notified and taken over by the Government.
The manager collected rent from the tenants at the reduced rates fixed under the rent-reduction regime.
A later ryotwari settlement fixed land-revenue rates that could exceed the reduced rent.
issues.conclusion: The appellants were entitled to the rent collected under the rent-reduction regime, and not to any excess land revenue resulting from the ryotwari settlement.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 3(4) of the Madras Estates Land (Reduction of Rent) Act, 1947, the lessee's preserved entitlement was to the reduced rent collected. Sections 16, 22 and 23 of the Andhra Pradesh (Andhra Area) Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act distinguish the assessment payable to the Government from rent payable to the lessee; a settlement assessment greater than the reduced rent does not enlarge the lessee's entitlement.

predicates.claim_by_lessee_for_rent_after_estate_no: A lessee claimed rent in respect of land after the estate containing it had been notified and taken over.
predicates.government_collected_reduced_rent: A government-appointed manager collected rent from the tenants at rates reduced under the applicable rent-reduction regime.
predicates.ryotwari_assessment_exceeded_reduced_ren: A later ryotwari settlement assessed land revenue at a rate greater than the reduced rent.

issues.definition: When a lessee claims rent after an estate has been notified, the manager has collected reduced rent, and the later settlement assessment is higher, the lessee's entitlement is limited to the reduced rent collected.

issues.legal_issue: The compensation rule for termination of a fixed-term right is consistent with a law requiring compensation to take account of the right's value and its unexpired term when the rule caps compensation at the lower of two income-based measures.
material_facts: The appellants' leasehold rights were terminated with 26 years of the lease period unexpired.
The governing Act required compensation to be determined having regard to the value of the right and the unexpired portion of its term.
The applicable rule limited compensation to the lesser of twenty times net annual income or net annual income multiplied by the unexpired term.
issues.conclusion: The compensation rule was not repugnant to section 20(2) of the Act; the unexpired term was a factor to be considered, not an exclusive multiplier that displaced the rule's cap.
issues.legal_principle: Section 20(2) of the Andhra Pradesh (Andhra Area) Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act requires compensation to be determined having regard to the value of the right and its unexpired term. Rule 1(ii), read with rule 2, sets an income-based limit for a fixed-term right. The statutory direction does not require compensation to be calculated solely by multiplying net annual income by the full unexpired term, and the rule is not repugnant to it.

predicates.compensation_for_terminated_fixed_term_r: Compensation is being determined for a fixed-term right that has been terminated.
predicates.governing_law_requires_consideration_of_: The governing law requires the decision-maker to consider both the value of the right and the unexpired part of its term.
predicates.compensation_rule_caps_award_at_lower_in: The applicable rule limits the award to the lower of two measures based on net annual income and the unexpired term.

issues.definition: If a fixed-term right is terminated, the governing law requires consideration of its value and unexpired term, and the compensation rule imposes the stated income-based cap, the rule is consistent with the governing law.

issues.legal_issue: The net annual income used to calculate compensation for a terminated leasehold right is based on rent payable to the lessee, not on a ryotwari settlement rate representing land revenue payable to the Government.
material_facts: The appellants' leasehold rights were terminated after a ryotwari settlement had been introduced in the lands.

For the three preceding fasli years used to determine average net income, reduced rent was payable under the rent-reduction regime in the earlier years, while the settlement rate applied in the last year.
The settlement rates represented land revenue payable to the Government, rather than rent due from the tenants to the appellants.
issues.conclusion: The Board correctly calculated net annual income using the rent fixed under the rent-reduction regime and did not use the ryotwari settlement rate.
issues.legal_principle: Rules 1(ii) and 2 made average net income during the three preceding fasli years the basis for compensation. The land-revenue assessment under section 22 of the Andhra Pradesh (Andhra Area) Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act represented what was payable to the Government and was not the rent due to the lessee. Section 3(4) of the Madras Estates Land (Reduction of Rent) Act, 1947 governed the rent entitlement preserved for the lessee.

predicates.compensation_based_on_average_net_income: Compensation for a terminated right is calculated by reference to average net income over the prescribed preceding years.
predicates.settlement_rate_represents_revenue_payab: The rate fixed by a later settlement represents land revenue payable to the Government, rather than rent payable to the lessee.
predicates.rent_reduced_under_applicable_rent_regim: The rent payable to the lessee was fixed under an applicable rent-reduction regime.

issues.definition: Where compensation depends on average net income, the settlement rate represents revenue payable to the Government, and reduced rent was payable to the lessee, the settlement rate is excluded from the lessee's income calculation.

issues.legal_issue: Cesses payable by a lessee under the lease are deductible in determining net annual income for compensation.
material_facts: The original patta required the lessees to pay local and other cesses payable by the ryots.
The relevant definition of rent included local taxes and cesses.
The Board deducted cesses from gross income when calculating net annual income for compensation.
issues.conclusion: The Board was justified in deducting the cesses payable by the lessees from gross annual income to determine net annual income.
issues.legal_principle: The definition of rent in section 3(ii) of the Madras Estates Land Act, 1908, incorporated into the Abolition Act by section 2(1), includes local taxes and cesses. Because the lease required the lessees to pay those cesses, net income for compensation purposes was calculated after deducting them from gross income.

predicates.compensation_based_on_net_annual_income: Compensation for a terminated right is calculated using net annual income.
predicates.lease_requires_lessee_to_pay_cesses: The lease requires the lessee to pay local or other cesses.
predicates.rent_measure_includes_local_cesses: The applicable measure of rent includes local taxes or cesses.

issues.definition: When compensation depends on net annual income, the lease makes the lessee liable for cesses, and the rent measure includes them, those cesses are deductible from gross income.

issues.legal_issue: A landholder is entitled to interest on rent collected by a government-appointed manager on the landholder's behalf and withheld from the landholder.
material_facts: The government-appointed manager collected rent from tenants on behalf of the appellants.
The collected rent was not paid to the appellants when collected and remained unpaid until a later payment.
The statutory collection framework required the manager to collect interest payable on rent arrears and to pay it to the landholder.
The appellants were deprived of the use of the collected rent.
issues.conclusion: The appellants were entitled to interest at 6% per annum on the rents collected by the manager on behalf of the Government and not paid to them.
issues.legal_principle: The Court applied general principles of equity and the Interest Act, 1839, under which interest may be awarded even where the governing statute does not expressly provide for it. The collection duty in section 55(1) of the Andhra Pradesh (Andhra Area) Estates (Abolition and Conversion into Ryotwari) Act included interest payable on arrears collected by the manager. The Court followed National Insurance Co. Ltd., Calcutta v. Life Insurance Corporation of India, [1963] Supp. 2 S.C.R. 971.

predicates.manager_collected_rent_for_landholder: A government-appointed manager collected rent from tenants on behalf of a landholder.
predicates.collected_rent_withheld_from_landholder: The manager or Government did not pay the collected rent to the landholder when it was collected.
predicates.landholder_deprived_of_use_of_collected_: The landholder was deprived of the use of the collected rent while it remained unpaid.

issues.definition: When a manager collects rent for a landholder, the collected rent is withheld, and the landholder is deprived of its use, interest is payable on that withheld rent.
